title: Local and quasilocal conservation laws of three-state IRF cellular automata and their quantum deformations
abstract: Using patch-matrix-product methods, we study two reversible three-state interaction-round-a-face cellular automata introduced by Klobas and Prosen [J. Phys. A 55, 094003 (2022)] - the species-preserving and species-flipping rules - and a coherent quantum deformation interpolating between them. Within an explicit translationally invariant ansatz, the two classical rules share a one-parameter family of quasi-local conservation laws with an auxiliary-dimension-three realization. Every regular member is also the first centered logarithmic derivative of an analytic auxiliary-dimension-two family passing through the identity observable. On the closed span of this family and the three elementary local charges, the only nonzero Euler velocities are $\pm\sqrt{3/23}$. Consequently, $\sqrt{3/23}$ is a rigorous lower bound on the maximal Euler speed in any larger conserved sector. For the species-flipping rule, this value agrees with the reported extrapolated value $0.361$ of Klobas and Prosen, strongly supporting completeness of the known sound-active charges. The species-preserving rule admits, in addition, a staggered generating family whose logarithmic derivatives form an infinite tower of strictly local charges. In the quantum deformation, the same algebraic structures yield exact low-bond-dimension invariant states (scar candidates), exponentially long-lived quasi-local quasimodes, and diagonal quasi-local charges that produce a nonzero Mazur bound after projection away from the three elementary local charges.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes the conservation laws of three-state IRF cellular automata and their quantum deformations using advanced matrix product methods. It establishes a lower bound on the system's maximal sound speed by analyzing conserved charges derived from both classical rules. The findings provide deep insights into the underlying integrability structure, particularly concerning the emergence of quasi-local invariants in the quantum regime.
main_problem: The study focuses on determining the local and quasilocal conservation laws governing three-state Interaction-Round-a-Face (IRF) cellular automata, both classically and through their quantum deformations.
main_result: The analysis established a rigorous lower bound for the maximal Euler speed ($\sqrt{3/23}$) for the species-flipping rule, strongly supporting the completeness of known sound-active charges. Furthermore, the quantum deformation yields exact low-bond-dimension invariant states (scar candidates).
method: The research employs patch-matrix-product methods (PMPA) combined with hydrodynamic projection techniques to analyze conserved quantities and their associated Euler velocities.
model_or_system: The model is a three-state IRF cellular automaton defined on a lattice, featuring two specific rules: species-preserving ($\chi_p$) and species-flipping ($\chi_f$). These classical systems are extended into a coherent quantum deformation.
key_observables: Quasi-local conservation laws, Euler velocities (e.g., $\pm\sqrt{3/23}$), low-entanglement invariant states, and the Mazur bound for diagonal quasi-local charges.
important_parameters: The analysis involves a one-parameter family of conserved laws and parameters related to the structure of the PMPA ansatz ($\lambda \in I^*$).
main_assumptions: The authors note that while they provide strong support for known sound-active charges, unconditional completeness of the full conserved space is not claimed.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates one time step of the IRF circuit using three-site gates; tables summarize the rules for $\chi_p$ and $\chi_f$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the classical conservation laws using PMPA, derives explicit algebraic forms for conserved quantities across multiple orders (Chunks 3 & 4), and then extends these findings to characterize low-energy states and charges in the quantum deformation.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework used to constrain conserved quantities in integrable or near-integrable lattice models is highly relevant to understanding dynamics in many-body quantum systems, particularly those exhibiting quasi-periodicity or emergent symmetries.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

Figure 2: Light-cone trajectories of the two classical rules from the same random lower- boundary initial condition. Species 1 and 2 are blue and red; vacancies are omitted (white).

(b) The physically relevant localization length of the connected quasi-local densities, ξdens = 2/[−log δ+]. The endpoint-centered bilinear form annihilates the γ± projectors exactly, and the full norm sequence obeys the two-root formula (63).

Figure 4: Support structure of the logarithmic tower. The displayed bars show the even- anchored classes of support 2n + 2; their reflected partners have support label 2n + 3 in the same fixed-anchor convention. The labels Qr refer to the canonical new conserved charge whose minimal support label in Ref. [5] is r. The first two log-derivative orders produce Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7 modulo lower-support charges.
